description: Issue summary: After a canary rollout that introduced a tokenizer change (progressive subword merges) for redwood-small-v2-tokenizer-v1, several FinSight requests previously pinned to the customer's explicit model version were routed silently to the legacy model variant. Impact: customer observed subtle response inconsistencies and a billing spike due to reprocessing; no explicit error returned to client, requests succeeded but used fallback model. Environment: production us-east-1; Dedicated/Enterprise tenant for FinSight. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use FinSight tenant token bound to a pinned model version for redwood-small-v2. 2) Issue identical prompt batches through the SDK client while shifting canary weight from 5% to 25% for the tokenizer-enabled variant. 3) Observe per-request token counts and routing decisions in the request traces. Observed behavior: When the tokenizer change produced different tokenization for identical prompts (differences in prefix token count and EOS placement), the runtime’s pinned-version matching (which relies on a request signature computed from canonicalized token stream) failed to find a matching affinity entry and quietly fell back to a compatible variant. Because the fallback path had trace-level backpressure suppression, no 5xx or 429 surfaced; response latency increased ~60ms on average and some outputs changed subtly (e.g., newline tokenization differences). Expected behavior: Pinned sessions should honor explicit model pins regardless of tokenizer divergence; if pin cannot be honored, system should surface an explicit warning/error to tenant and not silently route without audit. Logs/traces: see trace IDs in investigation_notes below. Postmortem risk: silent fallbacks can bypass audit trail and misattribute billing and quality regressions to pinned version.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Asha Patel (Support): FinSight reported that after our canary rollout they saw a batch of requests return responses that matched the legacy model despite an explicit version pin. Customer provided sample request IDs and a short trace; attaching here.

2026-03-10 10:04 - Marco Salazar (SRE): Initial triage: no 5xx/429s in tenant logs; observed unusual divergence in token counts between variants for same prompt. Opening ticket with infra and tokenizer team.

2026-03-11 02:30 - Elena Zou (Infra Eng): Found that affinity lookup uses a hashed canonical token stream produced by the tokenizer microservice. Canary variant altered the tokenizer merges which changed canonicalization; affinity lookup missed and fallback executed. Adding reproducer and traces to ticket.
2026-03-11 11:15 - Support (Asha): Notified customer of investigation and applied temporary monitoring alert to flag routing decisions where pinned=true and routed_variant!=pinned_variant.

2026-03-12 08:42 - Marco: Implemented a temporary audit log patch that records tokenization version in request metadata for pinned sessions. Rolling to prod us-east-1 as hotfix; monitoring during slow ramp.
2026-03-12 13:00 - FinSight (Customer): Confirmed they saw the audit metadata on subsequent requests; still seeing a handful of mismatches — requested ETA on a permanent fix.
investigation_notes: trace: us-east-1:trace-20260310-55a1c3 - request_id=ff12ab34 sample prompt 'Analyze quarterly revenue' - tokens: variant-A=28, variant-B=31 - affinity lookup failed (no pinned entry) - routed to fallback variant
Hypothesis 1: Tokenizer microservice returns non-deterministic canonicalization across variants; affinity key generation depends on exact token stream -> small changes break pin lookup.
Hypothesis 2: Orchestrator cache contains epochal entries keyed by tokenizer version; cache invalidation race during canary weight increase caused shard to present older tokenizer version metadata.

Reproducer: Deployed two tokenizer binary builds (stable and canary) to staging and ran 10k identical prompts through pinned session harness; observed 0.7% of requests dropped pin affinity when tokenizer mismatch present.

Related config: affinity-key = sha256(<tenant_id> + <model_version> + <tokenizer_version> + <first_16_tokens>) - tokenizer_version was not included in previous pin schema; changed behavior surfaced when tokenizer changed token counts across variants.

Temporary mitigation: patched proxy to include 'x-tokenizer-version' header from tokenizer-service in routing key to make affinity lookup tolerant (shim) and surfaced audit event when mismatch occurs.

Next steps: 1) Add tokenizer_version as required field in pin-generation schema and migrate active affinities (coord with orchestrator). 2) Build rollout presubmit test to detect tokenization deltas for pinned tenants. 3) Consider fallback policy: explicit error or enroll tenant into grace-mode when pin cannot be honored.
resolution: Workaround applied: shim to include tokenizer-version in routing metadata and audit mismatches (rolled 2026-03-12). Permanent fix in progress: update affinity schema to include tokenizer_version and run migration job to recompute pinned entries for active sessions; rollout plan pending CR approval. Customer asked for final ETA; target complete by 2026-03-19. Follow-up task INT-4412 created for migration orchestration.
resolution_status: Partial workaround deployed; permanent fix scheduled
